name: BMW DESIGN.md
tagline: A 544-line DESIGN.md token spec of bmw.com you drop in for a coding agent to follow
description: One brand folder inside VoltAgent's awesome-design-md, a 74-brand collection of DESIGN.md files that encode a real website's visual identity as agent-readable YAML front matter. The BMW file declares 27 color tokens (corporate blue #1c69d4, navy surface #1a2129), a 14-step BMW Type Next Latin type scale on weights 300 and 700, an 8-step spacing scale, a near-zero radius scale, and token specs for 26 named components from top-nav to cta-band-photo. You copy DESIGN.md into a project root and tell the agent to build against it. Meant for anyone who wants a coding agent to produce measured corporate-automotive UI instead of generic AI slop.
pricing_detail: Repo files are free under MIT. getdesign.md upsells a paid Website Starter Kit and Catalog Pass on top.
agent_guidance: Fetch the raw DESIGN.md from raw.githubusercontent.com rather than the GitHub tree page — the in-repo README is a stub that only points at getdesign.md. Use it as the token contract for a build, not as code: it names BMW Type Next Latin, which you do not have a license to, so map the family to a system-ui stack and keep the weight pairing (700 display / 300 body) and the 0px radius, since those two choices carry most of the look. Pair it with a component library you already trust (shadcn/ui, Base UI) and let this file drive only the theme layer.
why_it_matters: The parent repo is the de facto standard format for handing a brand's visual identity to a coding agent, and the BMW file is one of its most complete entries — a full token set plus per-component specs rather than a vibes paragraph.

name: Loftlyy — Apple
tagline: Apple's hex codes, type stack, SVG logos and do/don't rules, with a .md agent endpoint
description: Loftlyy is a brand-identity directory covering 83 companies; this is its Apple page. It gives four named colors with hex values and stated usage (#000000 black, #A2AAAD silver, #86868B space gray, #F5F5F7 off-white), the SF Pro and New York type stacks with weight lists and hosted woff2 URLs, three SVG logo variants (black, white, silver at 980x1210), and Apple's own do/don't trademark rules with a link to the official guidelines. The whole page is mirrored at /en/apple.md as a clean Markdown style reference with a ready-to-paste CSS variables block, and every brand is listed in /llms.txt.
agent_guidance: Do not scrape the HTML — append .md to any brand URL (curl https://loftlyy.com/en/apple.md) and you get the palette, a :root CSS variables block, font URLs and asset links in one small document; /llms.txt is the index of all 83 brands. For scripted work use the CLI: `loftlyy get stripe --output json | jq -r '.colors[0].hex'`. Treat it as an unofficial reference, not a license — the logos and typefaces here belong to the brands, so use them for study and internal mockups and swap in your own marks before anything ships.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few brand-reference sites built for machines first: an llms.txt index, a .md endpoint per brand, and a JSON-emitting CLI, which is exactly the shape an agent needs to theme a project against a known identity.
evidence: https://www.loftlyy.com/en/apple (curl, 200; WebFetch got 403), https://www.loftlyy.com/en/apple.md, https://www.loftlyy.com/llms.txt, https://www.loftlyy.com/en/cli, https://www.loftlyy.com/sitemap.xml, https://www.loftlyy.com/robots.txt, https://registry.npmjs.org/@loftlyy/cli

name: Watermelon UI Dashboards
tagline: Nine full React admin dashboards installed through the shadcn CLI from a public registry
description: The dashboards section of Watermelon UI, a free shadcn-compatible registry whose registry.json advertises 1,067 items (1,037 ui, 22 blocks, 5 hooks, 2 libs, 1 page). Each of the nine dashboards is a complete multi-page admin app — sidebar, topbar, theme provider, light and dark themes, and 15 to 22 files — installed with one `npx shadcn@latest add` call against registry.watermelon.sh. The wider site also ships 31 base components, 22 block categories with 187 individual blocks, and 158 animated components. Built on Base UI primitives with motion/react and lucide-react; MIT.

templates.name: Astrix Dashboard

agent_guidance: Reach for this when the user wants a whole admin surface in one shot rather than assembling one from shadcn/ui parts — a single `npx shadcn@latest add https://registry.watermelon.sh/r/<slug>-dashboard.json` drops in a working sidebar, topbar, theme toggle and populated pages. Two traps: the site is a client-rendered SPA that returns a 4KB shell to plain fetchers and 403s polite crawlers, so read https://registry.watermelon.sh/r/registry.json instead of the docs pages, and the per-item URL /r/<name>.json also serves the SPA shell, so validate the response is JSON before trusting it. Note the primitives are Base UI, not Radix, so mixing these files into an existing shadcn/ui project pulls in a second primitive layer; the animated components additionally pull motion/react.
why_it_matters: Free, MIT, shadcn-CLI-installable full dashboards are rare — most nine-app dashboard collections of this size are paid templates, and the machine-readable 1,067-item registry makes the whole thing directly usable by an agent.
evidence: https://ui.watermelon.sh/dashboards (curl 200; WebFetch 403, JS-only shell), https://ui.watermelon.sh/sitemap.xml, https://ui.watermelon.sh/assets/index-BIOz7Guc.js (dashboard manifest parsed from bundle), https://registry.watermelon.sh/r/registry.json, https://api.github.com/repos/WatermelonCorp/watermellon-registry

name: TUMFNX PDF Style Guide
tagline: Instagram post sharing formatting rules for PDF documents produced by Claude
description: A single Instagram post from TUMFNX presenting a style guide for PDF documents generated with Claude. It covers formatting and presentation conventions for the output. Content was captured out of band; the post itself was not fetched, and the depth and rigour of the guide are unverified.
agent_guidance: Treat this as a lead, not a source. Instagram will not serve the carousel text to a fetcher, so you cannot read the rules programmatically — if a user cites it, ask them to paste the slides. For real PDF output conventions from an agent, prefer a versioned document you control over a social post that can vanish.
why_it_matters: Marks a niche most design catalogs ignore — how an AI agent should style a document it generates, not a screen — but as an image-only social post it is a pointer rather than a usable reference.
evidence: Not fetched — instagram.com is excluded by task policy. Record built from the pre-supplied title, description and tags.

name: Clinora Icon (White)
tagline: White-fill SVG of the Clinora icon mark, for dark backgrounds
description: The white variant of the Clinora icon mark, served as a raw SVG from the clinora.ai brand asset directory. It is the icon-only lockup, not the full wordmark, and is intended for dark surfaces, app icons and favicons where the default mark would disappear. House brand asset — first-party, not a third-party resource.
agent_guidance: Use this file only inside Clinora's own surfaces, and pick it over clinora-icon.svg whenever the mark sits on a dark or photographic background. Inline the SVG rather than linking it if you need the fill to follow currentColor; do not recolor or redraw the path. It is not a general-purpose icon set — never suggest it for another project.
why_it_matters: First-party brand asset the owner needs on hand when an agent builds a Clinora surface, so it belongs in the index as a known-good source rather than something to be re-traced.
evidence: Not fetched — clinora.ai is the owner's own brand asset host and is excluded by task policy. Record built from the URL path and the pre-supplied metadata.

name: Clinora Icon
tagline: Default-fill SVG of the Clinora icon mark, for light backgrounds
description: The default variant of the Clinora icon mark, served as a raw SVG from the clinora.ai brand asset directory. It is the icon-only lockup rather than the full wordmark, and is the one to use on light or neutral surfaces; the white companion file handles dark backgrounds. House brand asset — first-party, not a third-party resource.
agent_guidance: This is the default Clinora mark — reach for it on light surfaces, and swap to clinora-icon-w.svg on dark ones rather than filtering or inverting this file. Pair the two behind a prefers-color-scheme rule or a single inline SVG driven by currentColor. Scoped to Clinora projects only; do not reuse it elsewhere.
why_it_matters: The canonical Clinora icon file, so an agent building a Clinora surface references the real mark instead of approximating it.
evidence: Not fetched — clinora.ai is the owner's own brand asset host and is excluded by task policy. Record built from the URL path and the pre-supplied metadata.
